guard_admission.enforced_by: code_review_bundle_guard.admission_exit_code, called by the runner AFTER the test session and INDEPENDENTLY of its result. A library can catch a refusal, substitute a fallback and let every test pass -- which is what retired N14-BUNDLE-010 -- so the exit code is not inferred from the test outcome.
guard_admission.first_initialization_tracking: ATTEMPTED at lifecycle START, not on completion. A module key is marked the moment its first eligible extent begins, so the extent that ends by RAISING has still spent the module's one chance. Reload, re-import, a retry after a failed initialisation, and any later call into an initialised module are all outside the extent.
guard_admission.native_resolution_extent: ctypes.* stays denied as a family, with one extent carved out: ctypes.dlopen and ctypes.dlsym are permitted only while a pinned RUNTIME module runs its FIRST normal initialisation on this thread, only when every Python frame between the call and that initialisation is runtime code or the interpreter's own import machinery, and only when the library resolves into the runtime tree or a protected system location.
guard_admission.not_claimed: co_filename is writable by code that builds its own code objects, so in-process adversarial code can forge RUNTIME provenance. That is the boundary the project already ratified (L6 R18) and this does not move it. What it does defend against is a refusal that changes execution semantics and is then absorbed by the caller.
guard_admission.prescribed_negative_controls: each sealed control DECLARES the refusal it is about to cause, before causing it, through guard.expect(event, contains, prescribed_by, why). The guard attributes every refusal against those declarations; anything unmatched is UNEXPECTED.
guard_admission.protected_system_locations: System32 and SysWOW64 under the SystemRoot read from HKLM through winreg -- not from the SystemRoot environment variable, for the same reason the review workspace stopped reading TMP.
guard_admission.provenance_source: WHERE CODE WAS LOADED FROM. A name supplied by executing code is not provenance, and generated or unregistered code -- anything without a real load location -- acquires none.
guard_admission.runtime_tree_untouched: the loader wrapping is an in-process wrapper on three importlib loader classes. No file in N14-RUNTIME-001 changes, and the runtime still re-hashes all 12002 of its own files at launch.
guard_admission.stop_condition: NOT 'a guard denial exists'. STOP on a launcher/runtime refusal, on a non-empty unexpected_denials, on a non-empty missing_prescribed_denials, or on an expected denial whose declaration does not match what happened.
guard_admission.thread_scope: extents are thread-local; a new thread inherits none. The attempted set is process-wide, because sys.modules is.

body: The previous package in this namespace asked you about the K axis
and declared the B axis open. Aaron stopped that dispatch,
authorised one further bounded repair, and it has landed. This
package asks about both.
**Do not narrow F02 to either axis.** They are independent
properties of the same frozen finding and they fail
independently:
* **A, the K axis** is the GRID channel. Per seed: K vs 2K, and
on failure the one authorized 2K vs 4K, then stop. It is
CONDITIONAL and bounded.
* **B, the B axis** is the MAIN channel. Per seed: B and 2B,
flat, unconditional, for all three governed seeds. There is no
4B and no further B escalation anywhere in the frozen
authority.
Confusing the two is the one mistake the final repair could have
made, so it is worth checking directly rather than reading the
comments: `tree/src/itsf/mc/mc_runner.py::_execute` builds the
B-axis arms, `::_witness` and `::_attempt` run the K-axis
escalation, and
`tree/src/itsf/mc/consumer.py::_convergence_rules_a_to_d` is
where rule (b) now takes both scales.
One structural choice the builder made that you should judge
rather than accept: the base seed's doubled-B arm is the
ratified `double_B`, filed under its own seed rather than
recomputed under a second label. The reason is M10's own compute
form -- three seeds x (base full + 2B full) -- which an extra arm
would overstate. If you think that reuse weakens the per-seed
property, say so: it is the one asymmetry left in the arm set.

body: Two of the test files in this package are both focused evidence
and, in one case, the home of the non-regression controls -- and
the repairs edited them. Saying exactly where is the point: a
control you cannot trust is not a control, and a fixture that was
adjusted to make its own subject pass is not evidence.
**`tree/tests/test_n14_round2_repairs.py`** (the first repair's
evidence, and the four controls) changed in three places, all
inside F02 and F04 tests, none in an F01/F03/F05/F07 test:
* two F02 tests follow the replacement of the single-witness
field by the attempt chain;
* `test_F04_test_only_grid_evidence_is_recorded_in_the_seal` was
replaced by `test_F04_the_seal_records_the_grid_evidence_kind`
and its assertion INVERTED, because the harness runs a
production-shaped prepared input and the authority that now
matches it is the production one. The old assertion encoded the
very pairing you found admissible.
**`tree/tests/test_n14_residual_repairs.py`** changed in exactly
one place for the final repair:
`test_F04_a_test_only_standing_is_refused_at_the_public_seal`
now also supplies the per-seed doubled-B arm set. Without it the
test received `seed_doubled_b_evidence_absent` instead of the F04
refusal it asserts. It asserts the same code as before.
**Treat that last change as a reason to probe F04 yourself**,
which the F04 target says in its own words. And for the four
controls: read their bodies in
`tree/tests/test_n14_round2_repairs.py` against the
F01/F03/F05/F07 BASIS sections in
`frozen/verify002/VERIFICATION_FINDINGS.md` and judge whether
they still assert what you verified. A control weakened to
accommodate a repair is a REGRESSED control and fails this
verification on its own.

body: Unchanged, and repeated because it is the one piece of contract
wording that had to be corrected before the first dispatch in
this arc.
A NEW concrete blocker that these repairs caused or exposed, in
the F02 / F04 / F06 / R1 seams they directly changed, **affects
the overall result**. It does not go in a footnote and it is not
separated from the outcome. R1 is the precedent: it was raised
exactly this way against the first repair and it is why F06 did
not close.
An observation that is genuinely unrelated -- pre-existing,
elsewhere in the tree, or reachable only by widening the search
-- goes in a clearly separated section and does NOT affect
closure. The line is mechanical: did these repairs introduce it,
in a seam they changed. The seams are the five production files
in section 1, measured from the commit you last verified.
**A reservation may not hide a material blocker.**
`CLOSED_WITH_RESERVATION` exists for a repair that closes the
stated failure path while leaving a NAMED narrower one open --
not as a softer way to report something that should block.

verification_targets.builder_claim: AXIS A: the witness minter had pinned the base arm to the frozen k and refused anything else, so the second comparison was inexpressible; it now admits `k = frozen x 2^d` for `0 <= d < max_doublings`, `_attempt` performs ONE authorized comparison, `_witness` loops only while the seed has not converged and breaks at the ruled bound, the standing consumes each chain's LAST attempt, and a chain continuing past a convergence is refused with `grid_convergence_retry_after_convergence`. AXIS B: `_execute` now builds a doubled-B arm per governed seed; the base seed's is the ratified `double_B` filed under its own seed rather than recomputed, so M10's compute form -- three seeds x (base full + 2B full) -- stays exact. Convergence REQUIRES the map and refuses absence, an incomplete seed set, an arm carrying another seed's master seed, a scale that is not exactly twice that seed's own base, and a redrawn world table, each with its own code. Rule (b) is now the conjunction of agreement at the base scale and agreement among the three doubled arms; rules (c) and (d) cover the new arms; the seal cold-replays them and records the coverage it consumed, and `RunnerResult.b_scales_by_seed` reports it as a final observable.
verification_targets.closure_requires: BOTH AXES, adjudicated separately and reported together. AXIS A (K): for every governed seed, K vs 2K; on a failed comparison the authorized 2K vs 4K and then stop -- no 8K. Each seed stops independently when it converges, reaches 4K only when required, and a seed still non-converged at the bound stays NON_CONVERGED and carries that into the cross-seed standing. No attempt after a convergence, no attempt beyond the ruled bound, the aggregate consumes each seed's FINAL legal attempt, and adjusted-map publication is still taken from the comparison the standing came from. AXIS B (B): seed 7, seed 13 and seed 31 each with B AND 2B. Each seed's doubled result is its OWN -- no seed inherits another's. Non-base 2B outcomes must affect the final standing: a disagreement visible only in seed 13's 2B arm must change final convergence, and the same for seed 31. Doubled-scale agreement is computed across all governed seeds. No 4B arm is invented, and the base seed's existing `double_B` semantics -- rule (a), the provenance relation, the world-prefix witness -- stay intact.

write_surfaces.base_is_not_a_read_root: the guard admits the frozen CHILD and nothing else outside the bundle and the runtime. The supplied base is stat'd, never listed: no sibling enumeration, no unrelated read, no part of it usable as review input.
write_surfaces.bytecode: sys.dont_write_bytecode is set by the runner itself, so nothing is written into the sealed tree or the runtime even if the runner is invoked without the launcher's -B.
write_surfaces.child_is_fresh: the child must not exist. It is refused even if it exists EMPTY, is never reused, and is never deleted by the runner: an empty directory is not evidence that it is unused, and removing another attempt's directory is worse than refusing.
write_surfaces.ephemeral_scratch: <review output root>/.scratch/ -- a dot directory beside the returns, never inside them. pytest's basetemp is pinned into it.
write_surfaces.forbidden_workspace_roots_note: DECLARED here because a sealed object cannot derive them from its own location. The sealed delivery, the review-delivery directory it sits in and the portable runtime beside it are DERIVED at runtime instead, so they stay correct if the delivery moves. Overlap is refused in both directions: a base inside one of these would put reviewer output in a governed place, and a base containing one would put a governed place inside the writable surface.
write_surfaces.output_binding: OUTPUT_BINDING.json in the child names REVIEW_ID, MANIFEST_SHA256, RUNTIME_MANIFEST_SHA256 and the substantive round. The runner refuses a workspace bound to any other review object, so one delivery's artifacts cannot be read as another's. The absolute path is execution provenance and is deliberately NOT part of the review identity: two seats may run this delivery at different paths and review the same bytes.
write_surfaces.read_boundary: the output root is an OUTPUT surface only. The guard admits that one directory and nothing else outside the bundle and the runtime, so temp siblings cannot be enumerated, read, or used as an input source.
write_surfaces.review_output_root: EXPLICITLY SUPPLIED BY THE DISPATCHER, never discovered. run_review.cmd requires --review-output-base <authorized writable base> and passes it to the runner, which canonicalises it, proves it is disjoint in BOTH directions from every forbidden root, creates exactly one FRESH child <base>/itsf-review/<REVIEW_ID>-<first 12 of MANIFEST_SHA256>, and proves CREATE/WRITE/RENAME/DELETE there by performing them. No default, no fallback, no environment read, no known folder, no profile inference: a missing parameter is a DELIVERY FAILURE before the guard arms. No username and no absolute workspace path enters the contract.

scratch_lifecycle.after_success: REMOVED by the runner, walking and unlinking
scratch_lifecycle.before: created empty by the runner inside the fresh child, before the guard arms. Nothing pre-exists it, because the child itself is new.
